::: {#fig-newton-quadratic}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: newton-quadratic-fig-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Contour plot of f(x) = (x1^2 + 3 x2^2) / 2 for x1 from -4 to 4 and x2
#|   from -2 to 2. The level curves are ellipses centred at the origin,
#|   wider along x1 than along x2. A point at (3, 1) lies on one ellipse. A
#|   vermilion arrow runs from that point straight to the origin, which is
#|   the Newton step. A grey arrow of the same length points along the
#|   negative gradient, down and left at 45 degrees, and does not reach the
#|   origin.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
nq_x1_nq <- seq(-4, 4, length.out = 101)
nq_x2_nq <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 101)
nq_grid_nq <- tidyr::expand_grid(x1 = nq_x1_nq, x2 = nq_x2_nq)
nq_grid_nq$z <- (nq_grid_nq$x1^2 + 3 * nq_grid_nq$x2^2) / 2
nq_newton_nq <- tibble::tibble(x = 3, y = 1, xend = 0, yend = 0)
nq_grad_nq <- tibble::tibble(x = 3, y = 1, xend = 0.764, yend = -1.236)
nq_start_nq <- tibble::tibble(x1 = 3, x2 = 1)
nq_arrow_nq <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.15, "inches"))
nq_aes_nq <- ggplot2::aes(x1, x2)
nq_z_aes_nq <- ggplot2::aes(z = z)
nq_seg_aes_nq <- ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)
nq_grid_nq |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  nq_aes_nq +
  ggplot2::geom_contour(nq_z_aes_nq, colour = "#0072B2", bins = 10) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    nq_seg_aes_nq,
    data = nq_grad_nq,
    colour = "grey50",
    arrow = nq_arrow_nq
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    nq_seg_aes_nq,
    data = nq_newton_nq,
    colour = "#D55E00",
    arrow = nq_arrow_nq
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = nq_start_nq, size = 2) +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x1", y = "x2")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: newton-quadratic-fig-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Contour plot of f(x) = (x1^2 + 3 x2^2) / 2 for x1 from -4 to 4 and x2
#|   from -2 to 2. The level curves are ellipses centred at the origin,
#|   wider along x1 than along x2. A point at (3, 1) lies on one ellipse. A
#|   vermilion arrow runs from that point straight to the origin, which is
#|   the Newton step. A grey arrow of the same length points along the
#|   negative gradient, down and left at 45 degrees, and does not reach the
#|   origin.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

nq_xx_py, nq_yy_py = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(-4, 4, 101),
                                 np.linspace(-2, 2, 101))
nq_z_py = (nq_xx_py**2 + 3 * nq_yy_py**2) / 2
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5), layout="constrained")
ax.contour(nq_xx_py, nq_yy_py, nq_z_py, levels=10, colors="#0072B2")
ax.annotate("", xy=(0.764, -1.236), xytext=(3, 1),
            arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "->", "color": "grey"})
ax.annotate("", xy=(0, 0), xytext=(3, 1),
            arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "->", "color": "#D55E00"})
ax.plot([3], [1], "ko")
ax.set_aspect("equal")
ax.set_xlabel("x1")
ax.set_ylabel("x2")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [level curves](vector-calculus.qmd#def-level-set) of $f$ in @exm-newton-quadratic are ellipses.
From the start $\tp{(3, 1)}$, the [Newton step](#def-newton-step) (vermilion arrow) goes straight to the [minimizer](algebra.qmd#def-global-minimizer) at the origin.
The negative [gradient](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative) $-\tp{(3, 3)}$ (grey arrow, drawn as long as the Newton step)
points across the narrow side of the ellipses and misses the origin.

:::
